name: Bloatmage — Additional Material (d20pfsrd)
body:
More on Bloatmage from d20pfsrd.com.

These sections appear on d20pfsrd.com's pages "Bloatmage", "Bloatmage" but are not part of the Bloatmage entry, which is unchanged.

From d20pfsrd.com: Bloatmage

Editor’s Note

Does a wizard (or other character that uses a spellbook), receive bonus spells to add to his spellbook when he gains a level in a prestige class that grants an increase to spellcasting?

No. The increase to his spellcasting level does not grant any other benefits, except for spells per day, spells known (for spontaneous casters), and an increase to his overall caster level. He must spend time and gold to add new spells to his spellbook.

Editor’s Note

On the Bloodsurge class ability chart it goes from 1d4 to 2d4 to 3d4 but the text progresses from 1d4 to 1d8 to 1d12. Normally “Text trumps table” but is it true in this case?.

After discussing this with James, we like the 1d4/1d8/1d12 option in the text better, as it makes it a little more risky for the reckless character–which makes the class more appealing if you’re a player who likes to take risks.

Note that if you play the class carefully, you’ll probably never rage if you use this ability. But sometimes an adventure requires you to push yourself a little harder than you’d planned….

From d20pfsrd.com: Bloatmage

Hemophilia (Ex)

Unlike normal spellcasters the bloatmage focuses on using their body to fuel their spells, sacrificing bits of themselves to do this. For the purpose of any arcane spellcasting classes the bloatmage has they use their Constitution modifier as their casting attribute in place of their original attribute (Intelligence for wizard, Charisma for sorcerer, etc.) and recalculate any DCs, spells per day, and so on taking this into account.

Blood Regulation (Ex)

At 3rd level, the bloatmage becomes adept at regulating their body from harmful ailments. If she is suffering from a disease or poison she can choose to spend 2 points from her blood pool in order to cure herself of the effect. If she is suffering from the nauseated condition she can instead spend 4 points from her blood pool to cure herself.

Exsanguinate (Ex)

At 4th level, a bloatmage learns to tie blood draining abilities to spells she casts. When spending blood points on spells instead of the normal effects the bloatmage can instead choose to start causing their enemies to rupture blood vessels and begin a vicious cycle of bleeding. This can only be put on spells which are single target and offer a Fortitude save. If the opponent fails the save, they take a number of bleed damage equal to the bloatmage’s bloodsurge die (maximum of 1d12 at 5th level).
